title: RSI
goal: Learn a 0 to 100 gauge of how fast a price moved.

objectives.text: Know that RSI goes from 0 to 100.
Know what the 70 and 30 lines mean.
Know that RSI can stay high or low.

slides.text: Momentum is how fast and how hard a price is moving. A quick climb with big candles has strong momentum.
slides.title: Momentum

slides.text: RSI is a gauge from 0 to 100. It reads the last 14 candles to size up momentum. It sits in a strip under the chart.
slides.title: The RSI gauge

slides.text: Overbought means the RSI is over 70. The price rose fast. A dotted line at 70 marks it.
slides.title: Overbought

demo.caption: Real Apple prices. The RSI went over 70.

slides.text: Oversold means the RSI is under 30. The price fell fast. A dotted line at 30 marks it.
slides.title: Oversold

demo.caption: Real Apple prices. The RSI went under 30.

slides.text: A high RSI does not mean the price must fall. A strong climb can stay overbought for weeks. Do not trust RSI alone.
slides.title: Not a stop sign

demo.caption: Real Apple prices. RSI stayed over 70 as price rose.

questions.explanation: RSI is a gauge of momentum. It shows how fast the price moved.

questions.prompt: RSI goes from which number to which?
An RSI over 70 is called overbought.
questions.explanation: Yes. Over 70 is overbought. Under 30 is oversold.

questions.prompt: The RSI is 25. What is it called?
questions.explanation: Under 30 is oversold. The price fell fast.

questions.prompt: Match each word to its meaning.

pairs.definition: How fast a price is moving

questions.explanation: RSI reads momentum. The 70 and 30 lines give two names.

questions.prompt: When the RSI is over 70, the price must fall now.
questions.explanation: No. A strong climb can stay overbought for a long time.

questions.prompt: What is a safe way to use RSI?

questions.explanation: RSI is one clue. Use it with other tools.
